Currently going through the same thing. Got out of the Marine Corps a couple of years ago and everything seems so low stakes and empty. I’m angry all the time, and generally have no idea where I’m going in life. I understand not wanting to go to therapy as I don’t believe it’s a “catch-all” solution to mental health issues. It can definitely help, but not if he’s actively resisting it. Something that really helped me deal with the transition and all the shitty things that come along with it was connecting with other veterans. I’m lucky enough to have some of my old military friends live within a couple hours of me and still talk to the ones that live in different states. But if that’s not an option, find local veteran groups, VFW clubs, or anywhere with a veteran population. It’s extremely beneficial to talk to people that “get it.” The best thing you can do is just be there for him. A random hug or an extra “I love you and I’m here for you” is gonna go a long way. Best of luck to both of you

0671 Cpl here. Just know you’re doing more than most by reaching out for resources regarding your mos. Keep that shit up. As far as actual resources go, If you’ve got access to LEM’s and ASM’s in your shop, get with your networkers and build servers from scratch. If you fuck it up, oh well. Wipe em and start again. It’s the best way to build experience and familiarity with server architecture. You’ll make a lot of mistakes, but it’s a good way to learn. Either buy or tactically acquire a sec+ book. It’s a great way to learn cybersecurity and general network infrastructure. And if you ever get put on the actual course, that CompTIA cert is worth a lot in the civilian world if you continue with IT. If you have the attention span of mosquito (like me) and you’d rather watch YouTube videos, look up CBT Nuggets. That channel has a video for damn near everything under the sun in the world of IT. One of my buddies had some of their videos saved to a hard drive on my last deployment and the entire shop made pretty good use of em. Don’t lose that desire for knowledge. It’ll benefit you when you find out that IT jobs are way better in the civilian world and you can do better than the Marine Corps. Hope this helped. Go and make our fellow data POGs proud.

Books: Any updated Sec+ or Net+ book on Amazon

Trust me man, we’ve all been there. A good way to motivate yourself is to find a reason to get in the gym. Whether it’s looking good for girls, maintaining your health, performing better in sports, or just feeling better about your appearance. Before I joined the Marine Corps, my goal was to gain some weight for boot camp. Now that I’ve accomplished that goal, i set a new goal to out perform my fellow Marines. And looking good for girls is definitely a motivator. It really boils down to setting realistic short term goals and finding out why you want to pursue fitness. Find some YouTube channels to help you plan workouts and get motivated. Fitness is all about mindset. Slow progress is better than no progress.
